Welcome to Buckswood
A Global School, in the Heart of the British Countryside.
As you explore our website, you are beginning a journey into a world where learning extends far beyond the classroom.
At Buckswood, we spark curiosity, build character, and nurture each student to become the best version of themselves.
Academics are first and foremost, but our school is about more than just academics. As you navigate the website, we hope you’ll gain a deeper understanding of our educational ethos, which is built on our ‘12 Pillars‘—a set of core values that guide everything from academics to personal development, resulting in well-rounded, passionate individuals who truly stand out. This is the Buckswood difference: an education that prepares students not just for success but for life.

Register below for one of our open events
Open days offer prospective parents the opportunity to visit the school, meet with staff and pupils and view the vast array of facilities we have to offer.
Experience the Buckswood difference first hand and discover what makes our learning environment so unique, receive a tour from one of our prefects to see a true reflection of life as a Buckswood student. Our open days occur at regular intervals throughout the school year. Each day time event starts at 10:00am and ends at 12pm, evening events commence at 5:30pm until 7:30pm.

BUCKSWOOD EDUCATIONADVENTURE & TRAVEL
We want our students to have zeal for life, have passion and not be afraid to try something new. Through the BEAT programme we want to challenge our students to challenge themselves, we instil a ‘can-do’ spirit of adventure in each scholar and encourage them to try something new, understanding that failure is not to be feared, knowing that new experiences make richer people.
For us to achieve this we run three very full programs.
The weekday after school activities program run by the ‘Not so boring office’ offer a very comprehensive set of activities that extend the curriculum outside the classroom.
The weekend activity program
Called REST (Saturday: School, coursework, outings, recuperation, Entertainment) and SCORE (Sunday: Rest, Enrichment, Sports, Timeout) provides the students with a fun packed weekend with trips out to London and areas of local interest and interhouse competitions that include interhouse sport, dance offs and fashion shows to name a few – there is no excuse to be bored!
Half Term travel: We run a very comprehensive travel program as we also believe that travel is the fourth dimension of education and places education in context, as we believe that it broadens minds and horizons, breaks down barriers, destroys misconception, enhances knowledge and promotes cultural understanding.

Start and End of Term Travel
Please note that boarders are expected to travel at the start and end of term at times that do not impact their learning. It is the school’s expectation that unless there is a compelling reason as to why a boarder is unable to travel at these times that arrangements are made by their family to ensure that they travel to or from school at the appropriate time and date. Travel to or from school is expected to be at the authorised dates and times only.
Any travel outside of these dates or times will be subject to a surcharge of £150 being levied on your school bill to cover the staffing costs incurred by the school for dealing with this inconvenience. To clarify this, the authorised times of arrival to school on a return to school day (Sundays after half terms and Mondays after longer holidays) are from 0900 until 2100 and the authorised times of departure from school prior to a holiday are from 1700 until 2100 on Friday afternoon or 0700 until 1200 on the Saturday morning at the end of term. It is expected that all boarders have left school (unless on a school trip) by 1200 on the Saturday at the end of a term as the school is then closed for the holiday and will not reopen for students until 0900 on the travel day at the end of the holiday. We advise that families use their guardians for travel taking place outside of these days and times when school is not in session.
Any late returns or early departures will also be marked as being unauthorised on the attendance record. Families are encouraged to book taxis through the school if transport to or from an airport or train station is required. If, however, they wish to use an alternate provider then this information must be clearly communicated to the school via the start/end of term travel form. This ensures that we know when and where all of our students are going and coming from at the start and end of each term. If you feel that you need to ask for an exemption from this, then this request must be made prior to any travel being booked so that the school can inform you whether or not this has been granted. Requests should be emailed to the relevant admissions representative.

Directions
How to find us.
Set in the beautiful East Sussex countryside we are easily accessible by road and rail, less than two hours from London, Gatwick and Heathrow.
Buckswood School,Broomham Hall,Guestling,East Sussex
TN35 4LT
Travelling by car
We are on the A259 between Hastings and Rye in the village of Guestling. From Hastings town centre take the A259 towards Rye and we are approx. 10/15 mins on the right, about 1 mile after you have passed through Guestling. From Rye town centre take the A259 towards Hastings and we are approx 15 mins on the left.
Travelling by train
The nearest station to the school is Hastings and there are direct services from London Gatwick and the Ashford International terminal. If travelling from London Heathrow, trains can be taken from the central London stations of Charing Cross (recommended), Victoria, Waterloo East, and London Bridge. We do not recommend that you arrive at Three Oaks.
Please check train times and fares here:National Rail
To arrive at the school from Hastings, you can take a Taxi from the stand at the station, a journey which will take approximately 15 minutes and cost approximately £10-12.

LEADERSHIP
Picture leading your team to victory in a house competition, organising an inspirational school event, or standing up to make your voice heard on issues you’re passionate about. Our Leadership Pillar is designed to give you the skills, courage, and platform to shine and be yourself!
At Buckswood, we’re all about sparking that can-do spirit and turning ideas into action, a dynamic journey where you can take the lead, navigating through challenges with confidence and creativity.
Through hands-on projects, teamwork challenges, and leadership roles across our diverse school activities, you’ll develop the resilience, empathy, and strategic thinking that real-world leaders are made of. It’s about more than just taking charge—it’s about inspiring others, making a difference, and having a fun while you’re at it.

MANNERS, APPROPRIATENESS, TRADITIONS
“Please”; “thank you”; “please – you first” – old fashioned values, out of date values?No, not at Buckswood.
When a scholar puts on their Buckswood school uniform they know the standards of behaviour that are expected of them. Through clear guidelines and clear expectations, a mature sense of worth, self discipline and good manners can be formed. Manners cost nothing but say so much about someone.
We have a programme whereby students have to step out of their comfort zone and have a go, preparing themselves for life… be it reading in assembly; preparing them for presenting in the future; to learning to dance (no one likes dad dancing at a wedding). Whatever it is, we want our students to feel comfortable in any situation. We promote the concept that scholars need to stand out from the crowd, need to be different, confident about who they are and know that they are their personal best. A Buckswood education teaches scholars not only to be confident but also to be persuasive and impressive in a public forum, to be a leader rather than a mere follower. We put the finishing touches to young ladies and gentlemen who leave with the panache to walk through any door, break down any barrier and flourish in their adult lives. This ‘finishing’ sees every Buckswoodian develop a decorum that is as at home in palaces as it is in a pauper’s home. A Buckswoodian commands respect and is respectful of others. Buckswoodians are as smart on the inside as they are on the outside in their striking gold trimmed blazers!

ACADEMICS
At Buckswood we are all on a learning journey, teachers, ancillary staff, scholars and managers alike. We see education as a scaffold of support for every student’s life progress and concerns can be tracked and individual pathways formed. We believe in a ‘learner centered’ approach to learning and the promotion of critical and creative thinking.
Academic life at Buckswood is well structured. Learners need structure; it gives them a sense of security, organisation and support. However, we challenge students to challenge themselves, also identifying strengths they didn’t know they had, builds their confidence and it is this confidence that is the key to their success in life. Buckswood has created an environment where everyone feels at home and is comfortable to raise their hand and ask questions; we want every student to be curious and approach learning as a journey of discovery.
A Buckswood education seeks to educate the whole child, our international family of nations widens every student’s horizons and developing within them a global understanding. We consider the written curriculum and planning to be the mainstay of who we are. Successful learning takes place when the taught curriculum aligns with the intention of the written curriculum. Curriculum strategy is an important part of our quest to learn along side our students

CHARITY
Every Buckswoodian knows that they have a duty to their community. At Buckswood, that community starts on campus and spreads across the globe. Our students know that they have to care for themselves, each other and their environment. As they come from all over the world, our charitable endeavours both here and abroad reflect our ethos of global citizenship and teach that the gift of giving brings many rewards. As a child travels through the difficult teenage years, there are many benefits to be gained by getting involved with helping other people and thinking beyond the end of their noses.
The Buckswood Foundation was set up to encourage students to participate in helping others overseas. The school owns its own Lodge in Swaziland where our students base themselves for their annual school charity trip to this most beautiful part of the world.
We make a living by what we get , but we make a life by what we give.

Home, boarding & wellbeing
Buckswood is a home. It is a working establishment, it is a school, and most importantly it is a place of learning and friendship. The connection between well-being and home underscores the importance of creating a supportive and nurturing environment that enhances physical, emotional, and social aspects of health and happiness. We believe that it is this sense of happiness and harmony that make the walls of the school stand strong as they are nourished by the laughter and happiness that exudes from the students. By prioritising the well-being of our school, we can cultivate a space that fosters growth, comfort and safety. Through the promotion of safety and wellbeing we are equipping our students with the tools of tolerance, resilience and maturity to cope with the world at large; be it being safe on the Internet to cultural appropriateness or general health and wellbeing.
The world outside school can be a ‘challenging’ place and we prepare our students to be able to face it equipped so, that they can flourish without fear of failure.

SPIRITUALITY
‘Spiritual’ is not synonymous with ‘religion’. At Buckswood, spiritual development is characterised by reflection through the understanding of valuing a non-material dimension to life, and you will find that all areas of the curriculum will contribute to a scholars’ spiritual development. We want individuals to have the opportunities to reflect on life’s fundamental questions and ‘special moments’ in their lives. Scholars need to be well informed so that they can ask questions and form opinions.
We live in such a busy world that we want our students to take full advantage of the beautiful campus on which we live and to find time for themselves, without their phones, so that they can find ‘balance’ which in turn will help them be wiser individuals.

SPORT
At Buckswood, we champion athletic excellence and sportsmanship through our diverse and comprehensive Sports Programme. Our students have access to a variety of sports including football, rugby, netball, hockey, tennis, swimming, volleyball, archery, golf, and basketball, ensuring opportunities for all interests and skill levels.
We offer specialist academies for football, rugby, riding, and golf, where students can receive advanced training and compete at various levels. Our facilities, including sports fields, 4G astro, Tennis courts, a swimming pool, and a gym, support a broad range of physical activities. Through participation in local, regional, and national tournaments, as well as physical education classes, students not only enhance their athletic abilities but also develop crucial life skills such as teamwork, leadership, and resilience.
